# `Q-16-8` — Ambiguous project type extension

> A bare `project.type` name matched more than one extension
> contributing a project type.

## What this means

Extensions are identified by `organization/name`, but `project.type`
accepts the bare `name` as a convenience. When two installed extensions
contribute a project type with the same bare name, that convenience
becomes ambiguous.

Quarto picks one and tells you which, rather than failing: the
extension with no organization wins, and among organization-qualified
candidates, the lexicographically first organization wins. The message
names both the chosen extension and the ones it shadowed.

The render continues with the chosen type. The risk is that the choice
is not the one you meant, and the resulting project is configured by
the wrong extension — a failure that shows up as puzzling output
rather than as an error.

## Why this happens

- **Two extensions with a generic type name** — `docs`, `site`,
  `report` — from different organizations.
- **A vendored copy alongside an installed one.** An extension copied
  into `_extensions/<name>/` while the same extension is also
  installed under `_extensions/<org>/<name>/`.
- **A fork.** You forked an extension, installed the fork under your
  own organization, and left the original in place.

## How to fix

Use the full `organization/name` form so the choice is explicit:

```yaml
project:
  type: my-org/docs
```

This is worth doing even when the current default happens to be right —
installing another extension later can change which candidate wins,
and the bare form gives no signal when that happens.

If one of the candidates is a leftover, remove it:

```bash
quarto remove <owner>/<name>
```

or delete its directory under `_extensions/`.
